sources: dossier=Net position ('AbandonCandidate...on failure paths - leaf failure, strict-cancel from a sibling, backfill abort') and Required behaviors ('Backfill honors partition-selector overrides...', tagged artifact-only, i.e. still an open/undelivered promise as of dossier date); doc=invariant line 23 named triggers 'failure / strict-cancel / backfill-abort'; code=terminal_decision.go:33-54 defines exactly three abandon outcomes (OutcomeAbandon/natural, OutcomeAbandonSiblingCancel, OutcomeAbandonDescendantCancel), all routed through the single AbandonCandidate call at terminal_decision.go:181; rg -i backfill across lib/cmd/test finds zero backfill dispatch/cancel flow, only an orphaned CLI grant and unrelated migration-backfill SQL comments; test=runner_subclaim_test.go asserts AbandonCandidate fires on OutcomeAbandon.
note: The doc's status is as-is (current-state only), but backfill is not implemented anywhere in the codebase and the dossier's own Required-behaviors section frames backfill support as an unfulfilled, artifact-only-tier open promise - not a delivered trigger. Naming it as a current invariant violates current-state-only doc convention, and the doc omits the real third trigger (descendant-cancel) that the fan-out cancel path exercises today. Replaced 'backfill-abort' with 'descendant-cancel' in the trigger list; backfill remains unmentioned per its open-promise status (not an intentional absence, just not yet built - queued as fix-code territory for the code gap itself, outside this doc-only mandate).

sources: dossier=Net position: 'Candidate lifecycle is pinned to claim-tree events' (claim-based framing, not run-based); doc=Boundaries line 17 and Invariant line 24 both said 'parent-run terminal flow'; code=SettleFromFanoutChild (child_execution.go) and CheckAndFireResolution/auto_terminal.go gate aggregation on 'all holders inactive AND CommittedChildrenCount+AbandonedChildrenCount >= ExpectedChildrenCount' - a parent-CLAIM resolution condition that a late child settlement can fire after the parent run itself already terminated.
note: The label 'parent-run terminal flow' misleads a reader into placing the aggregation trigger at the parent node run's terminal specifically, when it actually fires at parent-claim resolution (which can postdate the parent run's own terminal). The underlying invariant text was already precise about the actual condition; only the label was imprecise. Renamed to 'parent-claim resolution' in both Boundaries and the Invariants heading for consistency.

sources: dossier=Net position: 'the protocol carries only control-plane methods' and 'Data motion is substrate-direct via the ClaimResult address'; no dossier bullet anywhere describes a runtime data-block delivery to the producer; doc=invariant line 25 parenthetical 'consulted at runtime per producer state'; code=spec.NodeClaimProducerRef.Data is consumed only by ValidateClaimProducer at template registration (validation_pipeline.go) and template-equality comparison; claimproducer.ClaimSpec and the proto OpenRequest carry no data field at all, so there is no wire path for a data-block to reach a producer at runtime.
note: No intent source, dossier or code, describes any runtime delivery of the data-block to the producer - the dossier's own control-plane-only framing and the absence of any data field on the runtime protocol messages both rule this out. Removed the unsupported 'consulted at runtime per producer state' parenthetical; the invariant now states registration-time-only parsing.

sources: dossier=Net position: candidate handle is 'inert bytes...lives on sub-claim rows only, stored and passed verbatim...reaches the leaf executor inside the existing per-claim address structure of ExecuteRequest' (describes storage/passing, not an explicit doc-ownership split); doc=data-processing.md Boundaries line 17 said 'Owns: ...the producer-candidate-handle lifecycle on sub-claim rows' with no disambiguation from fan-out's own Boundaries line, which separately claims 'the per-child producer-candidate handle for data-processing-capable producers'.
note: Both docs read as owning the same artifact because neither states the split explicitly, even though the split (fan-out threads the handle through per-child dispatch; data-processing owns the begin/commit/abandon value-transition semantics of that handle) is inferable and non-contradictory from the dossier's own framing. Reworded data-processing.md's Owns clause to 'the producer-candidate-handle's value-transition lifecycle (begin / commit / abandon)' and added an explicit Does-NOT-own line for 'the per-child threading of the producer-candidate handle through fan-out dispatch (see concept:fan-out)'. fan-out.md itself was not edited (out of scope for this ruling) - if its wording still reads as competing ownership after this change, that's a follow-up for the fan-out cluster.

sources: dossier=silent on the term 'ledger' vs 'projection' for lineage; design corpus=concepts/lineage.md, but the row's quoted evidence ('the lineage projection is a materialized view rebuildable from...') is the PRE-edit text - a concurrent uncommitted edit to lineage.md (visible in git diff at adjudication time, matching phase1-rulings-lineage.jsonl row 449's fix-doc ruling) has already replaced that framing with 'written forward from...at terminal time, not reconstructed from them', explicitly append-only and forward-written - properties that align with, not contradict, 'ledger' terminology.
note: The finding's factual premise (lineage.md insists on a rebuildable-materialized-view framing that clashes with 'ledger') no longer holds against the current lineage.md text, which now emphasizes append-only, forward-written, non-reconstructable semantics - compatible with ledger language. Lineage remaining explicitly non-source-of-truth (audit log is) is a separate, weaker nuance not sufficient on its own to force a terminology change here. No edit applied; left 'lineage ledger' as-is in data-processing.md.
